originalSourceText:
Q.9  A robot nearly collides with a worker, but no injury occurs. The engineering team
       decides not to record the event because "nothing happened." Which principle is
       violated?

      (A) Near-misses should be logged and reviewed

      (B) Data should always be deleted

      (C) Simulation should replace testing

      (D) Learned components should control safety-critical paths

       Explanation: The safety standards explicitly recommends logging and reviewing every
       near-miss or unexpected behaviour, even when no harm occurs.

      Refer slides20, 21 of lecture 60: Application Domains, Ethics, Safety, Future of AI
       Robotics, Course Review & Career Pathways
